title: Errands
goal: Get everyday jobs done around town on your own: take out cash, pay a bill, get copies made, buy medicine, sort out a SIM and a top-up, get your phone fixed, clothes stitched and ironed, your hair cut and a parcel sent.
intro:
Living in Pune or Mumbai means errands: the ATM that's out of cash, the queue at the bank, the copy shop, the chemist's, the cracked phone screen, the tailor, the barber, the clothes that need ironing, the parcel for your mum. Most of these jobs are done for you by someone at a small local shop, and the key pattern for that is **-ऊन घेणे** 'get it done': not दुरुस्त केला 'I fixed it' but दुरुस्त **करून घेतला** 'I got it fixed'.

In this unit you'll learn to say what you need to get done, ask someone to do it for you (**करून द्या**, **करून मिळेल का?**), and ask the question every errand ends with: **कधी तयार होईल?** 'When will it be ready?'

grammar.title: Getting it done: -ऊन घेणे and -कडून
grammar.body:
English says *I got my hair cut* or *I'm having a shirt made*. Everyday Marathi does this with two verbs: the job verb in its **-ऊन** form ('having done') + **घेणे** 'take'. Literally 'have it done and take it' — the job is done for **you**.

दुरुस्त करणे 'repair' → दुरुस्त **करून घेणे** 'get repaired'
कापणे 'cut' → **कापून घेणे** 'get cut'
शिवणे 'stitch' → **शिवून घेणे** 'get stitched'
बदलणे 'change' → **बदलून घेणे** 'get changed / replaced'
धुणे 'wash' → **धुऊन घेणे** 'get washed'
तपासणे 'check' → **तपासून घेणे** 'get checked'

**Making the -ऊन form:** stem + ऊन: कर → करून, काप → कापून, शिव → शिवून, काढ → काढून; vowel stems add -ऊन: घे → घेऊन, दे → देऊन, धु → धुऊन, जा → जाऊन.

**Who does the work** takes **-कडून** on the oblique: मी **शिंप्याकडून** शर्ट शिवून घेतला 'I had the tailor make a shirt'. Often you leave the person out.

**Tenses:** only घेणे changes. Present: मी केस कापून **घेतो**. Want to: मला फोन दुरुस्त करून **घ्यायचा** आहे. Past: घेणे is transitive, so it follows the ergative rule from Unit 16 and agrees with the **thing**: शर्ट शिवून **घेतला** (m), स्क्रीन बदलून **घेतली** (f), केस कापून **घेतले** (pl).

**The trap:** मी शर्ट **शिवला** means *I* sewed it. At the tailor's it's **शिवून घेतला**. (With haircuts people often just say केस कापले — everyone knows you didn't do it yourself — but कापून घेतले is never wrong.) Marathi also has true causative verbs (करवणे, करवून घेणे), but they sound bookish; -ऊन घेणे is what you'll hear.

examples.en: She's having a dress made at the tailor's.
Get these clothes washed at the laundry. (informal)
I had the doctor check everything.

grammar.title: Asking for the job: करून द्या, करून मिळेल का?, -ला देणे
grammar.body:
Three patterns cover almost every conversation at a counter.

**1. -ऊन + देणे = do it for someone.** The mirror image of -ऊन घेणे: घेणे is 'for myself', देणे is 'for you / for them'. You ask: दोन झेरॉक्स **काढून द्या**, पत्ता **लिहून द्या** 'write the address down for me'. The shopkeeper answers: उद्या **करून देतो** 'I'll do it for you tomorrow'. With a friend: **करून दे ना**.

**2. -ऊन + मिळेल का? = can I get it …-ed?** Literally 'will it be got, done?'. It's the politest, most natural way to ask whether a shop does something and whether it can be done in time: हे दुरुस्त **करून मिळेल का?** · आज संध्याकाळपर्यंत **करून मिळेल का?** · इथे झेरॉक्स **काढून मिळेल का?** The answer is usually **मिळेल** 'yes, you can' or **नाही मिळणार** 'no'.

**3. noun + -ला + देणे / टाकणे = give in for a job.** फोन **दुरुस्तीला दिला** 'I gave the phone in for repair', कपडे **इस्त्रीला दिले**, कपडे **धुवायला टाकले** 'I put the clothes in the wash'. With a verb you use the -आयला form (Unit 15): **धुवायला**, **कापायला**.

Then comes the question: **कधी तयार होईल?** / **किती वेळ लागेल?** and the classic answers **संध्याकाळपर्यंत होईल**, **उद्या या**, **तासाभरात करून देतो**.

examples.en: Write this down for me, please.
Can I have it done by this evening?
I've given my phone in for repair.
I've put the clothes in the wash.

examples.native: काळजी करू नका, उद्या करून देतो.
examples.roman: kāḷjī karū nakā, udyā karūn deto.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'll have it done for you tomorrow. (shopkeeper)

grammar.title: I need to…: -आयचा / -आयची / -आयचे आहे
grammar.body:
You met मला जायचं आहे 'I need / want to go' in Units 15 and 17. When the verb has an **object**, the -आयचा part agrees with that object, exactly like an adjective (and like the ergative past):

मला फॉर्म भरा**यचा** आहे — फॉर्म m
मला सही करा**यची** आहे — सही f
मला खातं उघडा**यचं** आहे — खातं n
मला पैसे काढा**यचे** आहे**त** — पैसे m pl
मला गोळ्या घ्या**यच्या** आहे**त** — गोळ्या f pl
मला तिकिटं काढा**यची** आहे**त** — तिकिटं n pl

With a plural object, आहे becomes **आहेत**. With no object (go, come, sleep) it's always neuter: मला **जायचं** आहे.

**Spoken forms:** the आहे fuses on: काढायचं आहे → **काढायचंय**, भरायचा आहे → **भरायचाय**, करायची आहे → **करायचीय**, काढायचे आहेत → **काढायचेत**.

**Past:** होता / होती / होतं / होते = 'was supposed to': मला बिल भरायचं **होतं** 'I was meant to pay the bill'.

**The trap:** don't let the dative मला make you think of 'I' — the ending follows the **thing**. You will hear many people, especially in Mumbai, use the neuter -आयचं for everything (मला पैसे काढायचं आहे); that's fine in fast speech, but the agreeing form is the standard one.

examples.en: I need to buy new sandals.
What do you want to get? (informal)
We need to buy two tickets.
She needs to send some money home.

examples.native: मला आज बिल भरायचं होतं, विसरलो!
examples.roman: malā ādz bil bharāytsaṃ hotaṃ, visarlo!
examples.en: I was supposed to pay the bill today — I forgot! (man)

dialogue.title: Saturday errands
dialogue.setting: Saturday morning on FC Road in Pune. Neha bumps into her friend Aditya, who has a list of jobs to do — and a cracked phone.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper

lines.roman: miḷel nā. orijinal pāhije kī kôpī?
lines.en: Sure. Do you want an original or a copy?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.en: Original is four thousand, the copy eighteen hundred.

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: कॉपी घे रे, फोन तसाही जुना आहे.
lines.roman: kôpī ghe re, fon tasāhī dzunā āhe.
lines.en: Get the copy — the phone's old anyway.

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.en: OK, the copy. When will it be ready?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: तासाभरात करून देतो. तोपर्यंत बाकीची कामं करून या.

lines.en: I'll have it done within the hour. Go and do your other errands in the meantime.

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: चल, मग आधी शिंपी, मग बँक. आणि नंतर वडापाव!
lines.roman: tsal, mag ādhī shimpī, mag bæṅk. āṇi nantar vaḍāpāv!
lines.en: Come on then — tailor first, then the bank. And then vada pav!

culture: Most errands in Maharashtra happen at small neighbourhood shops where the same people know you for years: the **मेडिकल** on the corner (nobody says 'pharmacy'), the **झेरॉक्सचं दुकान** that also prints, laminates and fills in online forms for you, the mobile shop that does recharges, SIMs and repairs, the **शिंपी**, the **सलून**, and the **इस्त्रीवाला** with a heavy iron at a table under a staircase. Men behind the counter are **दादा** or **काका**, women **ताई** or **मावशी**; you can drop to **तू** with the ones you see every week (दादा, जरा लवकर करून दे ना), but stay with **तुम्ही** in a bank or a smart salon. Services are rarely bargained over — always ask **कधी तयार होईल?**, and know that the tailor's 'उद्या नक्की' ('tomorrow, for sure') often means the day after. In Pune be ready for the famous afternoon closing (many shops shut roughly from one to four) and the witty, slightly grumpy signs (**पुणेरी पाट्या**) telling you not to ask for change or credit. Almost everywhere you can pay by UPI: **स्कॅन करू का?** 'shall I scan?' A new SIM needs ID — Aadhaar for Indians, passport and visa for foreigners.

lessons.title: At the bank and the ATM

tip.title: मला फॉर्म भरायचा आहे — need to, agreeing with the thing
tip.body:
- **मला + thing + stem-आयचा + आहे** = 'I need to…'. The -आयचा part agrees with the **thing**: फॉर्म भरा**यचा** (m), सही करा**यची** (f), खातं उघडा**यचं** (n), पैसे काढा**यचे** आहे**त** (pl).
- No object → neuter: मला बँकेत **जायचं** आहे.
- Spoken: काढायचे आहेत → **काढायचेत**.

sentences.en: I need to go to the bank.
I want to open a new account.
I need to fill in this form.
How much do you want to take out?
I need to pay my phone bill.
I need to pay some money into my account.
This ATM's out of cash too!

sentences.roman: ādz bæṅk band āhe, udyā dzāūyā.
sentences.en: The bank's closed today, let's go tomorrow.
Have you got any cash? (informal)

tip.title: काढून द्या — do it for me
tip.body:
- **stem-ऊन + द्या** = 'please do it for me': झेरॉक्स **काढून द्या**, पत्ता **लिहून द्या**. With a friend: **करून दे ना**.
- **stem-ऊन + मिळेल का?** = 'can I get it done?': इथे झेरॉक्स **काढून मिळेल का?**
- The shopkeeper: **करून देतो** 'I'll do it for you'.
- -ऊन form: कर → करून, लिहि → लिहून, घे → घेऊन.

sentences.en: Three copies of this, please.
Have you brought a copy of your ID?
Write me a receipt, please.
Can I get photocopies done here?

sentences.native: मला हा फॉर्म भरून द्याल का?
sentences.roman: malā hā fôrm bharūn dyāl kā?
sentences.en: Could you fill in this form for me?

sentences.native: सही इथे करा आणि नाव इथे लिहा.
sentences.roman: sahī ithe karā āṇi nāv ithe lihā.
sentences.en: Sign here and write your name here.

sentences.native: रांग खूप लांब आहे, आपण उद्या येऊया का?
sentences.roman: rāṅg khūp lāmb āhe, āpaṇ udyā yeūyā kā?
sentences.en: The queue's really long — shall we come tomorrow?

I'll have it done for you in two minutes. (shopkeeper)

lessons.title: At the chemist's and the phone shop

tip.title: हवंय, नाहीये, काढायचेत — how it's really said
tip.body:
- In speech आहे fuses onto the word before: हवं आहे → **हवंय**, हवी आहे → **हवीय**, संपला आहे → **संपलाय**.
- आहेत after a vowel → **-एत**: काढायचे आहेत → **काढायचेत**.
- नाही आहे → **नाहीये** 'there isn't (right now)'.
- Use the full forms when writing or being careful; the short ones with friends and at the counter.

sentences.en: Have you got the doctor's prescription?

sentences.native: हे औषध आता नाहीये, संध्याकाळी या.
sentences.roman: he aushadh ātā nāhīye, sandhyākāḷī yā.
sentences.en: We haven't got this medicine right now, come back in the evening.
Is there a chemist's anywhere nearby?
I need something for a fever. (lit. a fever tablet)
My plan has run out.
You'll need ID for a new SIM.

sentences.en: I need to take out some money — where's the ATM?

sentences.roman: mī meḍikalmadhye āhe, kāhī havaṃy kā?
sentences.en: I'm at the chemist's — need anything?

tip.title: दुरुस्त करून घेतला — I got it fixed
tip.body:
- **stem-ऊन + घेणे** = get it done (for yourself): दुरुस्त **करून घेणे**, स्क्रीन **बदलून घेणे**.
- The person who does it takes **-कडून**: मित्रा**कडून** फोन दुरुस्त करून घेतला.
- In the past घेणे agrees with the thing: फोन **घेतला** (m), स्क्रीन **घेतली** (f).
- Trap: मी फोन दुरुस्त **केला** = I fixed it myself.

sentences.native: माझ्या घराजवळ एक चांगलं सलून आहे.
sentences.roman: mājhyā gharādzavaḷ ek tsāṅglaṃ salūn āhe.
sentences.en: There's a good salon near my place.
Just a shave, please.

sentences.native: मागून बारीक करा, पुढे थोडे जास्त ठेवा.
sentences.roman: māgūn bārīk karā, puḍhe thoḍe dzāst ṭhevā.
sentences.en: Short at the back, leave a bit more at the front.

sentences.native: शिंपी म्हणाला की कपडे सोमवारी तयार होतील.
sentences.roman: shimpī mhaṇālā kī kapḍe somvārī tayār hotīl.
sentences.en: The tailor said the clothes will be ready on Monday.

sentences.native: केस खूप वाढलेत, आज कापून येतो.
sentences.roman: kes khūp vāḍhlet, ādz kāpūn yeto.
sentences.en: My hair's got really long — I'll go and get it cut today. (man)
Give these shirts in for ironing, will you? (informal)
I need to pick up the clothes from the laundry.

sentences.native: ही साडी लॉंड्रीत धुऊन घ्यायची आहे.
sentences.roman: hī sāḍī lôṇḍrīt dhuūn ghyāychī āhe.
sentences.en: I want to get this sari washed at the laundry.
You'll get the clothes the day after tomorrow.
Will this parcel get there by tomorrow?
How much is the courier?
I sent Mum some books by courier.
Write the address on the parcel in English.
How much do you charge for ironing?
Has my parcel come?
